items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Wilbur Sweatman, he was vaudeville, he played three clarinets at one time, but he used a piano and a trumpet and drums. So he had this engagement at the Lafayette Theatre and so I got that gig for us.

ctx.x: I'm 17 now, and anyway -- wait a minute -- anyway, we come to New York, so me and Duke had a room together. I had an aunt in New York, got a room. I think I was giving her about $3.00 a week. We had adjoining rooms for $3.00 a week, so me and Duke had adjoining rooms. Duke ain't never been to no New York. He ain't never seen no building as tall as that in his life.

So man, I told him -- cut that -- (Recording interruption) So now we're in New York and we're just gigging, nothing steady, so we get a job -- Wilbur Sweatman, he was vaudeville, he played three clarinets at one time, but he used a piano and a trumpet and drums. So he had this engagement at the Lafayette Theatre and so I got that gig for us. I got that for us, we played around New York, in New Jersey

but he worked on Keith's Circuit too, but it was just four of us on the stage and him and he played clarinet, three of them at one time. Beautiful. Stage setting, he had a beautiful stage setting, whole lot of drapes, but we used to have to get to the theatre an hour before showtime to get made up.
